topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture’s aims and connects its study of cancer genetics to the histopathology practicals.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how studying tumor-causing viruses established that cancer can originate from altered normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental assays of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how experiments test whether genes and mutations confer transformed properties on cells.

topics.label: Functional classification and effects of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects, using cell-cycle regulation and dominant-negative p53 to illustrate and qualify those classifications.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defects in DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish sequence from chromosomal instability and explain how failures to repair DNA damage produce those phenotypes.

topics.label: Genetic instability from replication and mitotic errors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how errors in transmitting the genome during cell division generate instability and alter cancer-cell behaviour.

topics.label: Mutation timing in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing and order of mutation acquisition, especially genetic instability, affect colorectal tumor development.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and the limits of instability dependence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow inherited cancer-predisposing mutations from accelerated tumor development to the BRCA2 example showing that an established cancer need not retain its original repair defect.

topics.label: Lecture close, further reading and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the learning outcomes and offers questions, reading and a preview of the next lecture.
